resources.string: Microglial surveillance
How microglia patrol brain tissue

Normal surveillance and one example of local cleanup. Live imaging in mice informs the surveillance scene; the cleanup sequence is based on normal cell turnover in the adult mouse hippocampus. Timing and scale are schematic.
A resident in brain tissue
Microglia live among neurons and other glial cells. At baseline, a compact cell body sends out thin, branching processes into the surrounding tissue.
Moving tips survey the surroundings
Even in the so-called resting state, the tips extend and retract at different times. The cell body can stay in place while the branches sample nearby tissue.
A branch reaches local debris
Normal cell turnover leaves material to clear. In this example, a nearby microglial process reaches a small piece of that material without the whole cell moving toward it.
A pouch closes around the debris
The process wraps a pocket of its membrane around the material. When the pocket closes, it holds the debris inside the cell. This is phagocytosis.
The cell breaks down what it took up
The inset shows the captured material being broken down inside the cell. Other tips keep moving through their local surroundings.

Ramified microglia in brain tissue
Microglial cell body
The compact cell body gives rise to several thin processes and often stays in place during baseline surveillance.
Elongated nucleus
The nucleus sits within the compact cell body; it can appear elongated in a tissue section.
Process fork
A larger process divides into finer branches that reach different parts of the surrounding tissue.
Fine process tip
Fine ends can extend and retract even while the cell body stays put.
Nearby neuron
Microglial branches reach into the neural tissue around neurons; they are not extensions of the neurons themselves.
